key_insight: An unfitted FEM for elliptic PDEs uses PHT-splines on hierarchical T-meshes and solves a least-squares-style residual minimization over a neighborhood of the domain, avoiding cut-cell geometry.
engineering_relevance: The method enables accurate, stable simulations on complex level-set boundaries using only the background mesh and standard quadrature, which simplifies implementation for engineering models.
method: Builds on smooth PHT-spline spaces over hierarchical T-meshes.
Formulates the PDE by minimizing the L2 residual over an extended domain neighborhood.
Uses residual-based a posteriori indicators for adaptive local refinement.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports well-posedness, optimal H1 a priori error estimates, and numerical experiments that confirm accuracy and efficiency.
watch_item: Performance still depends on good adaptive refinement and accurate level-set representation; very complex geometries may require careful mesh resolution.
paper_title: UnCut FEM with PHT-splines on unfitted T-meshes
